builds.name: Reference: Ranked support core
builds.goal: Reference for Karma: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ support players use most (3,711 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 55.9% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A flexible poke and protection mage who chooses between empowered damage, tether healing and multi-ally shields. The current support provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Echoes of Helia → Moonstone Renewer → Redemption. Summon Aery keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Ionian Boots of Lucidity, Dream Maker, Dawncore.
builds.summary: The proven support baseline: Echoes of Helia → Moonstone Renewer → Redemption, with Summon Aery.
testPlan: Play it in support as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Echoes of Helia → Moonstone Renewer → Redemption) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 55.9% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Echoes of Helia → Moonstone Renewer → Redemption.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.

kitEvidence.formula:
Karma begins the game with a point in {{Spell_KarmaMantra_Name}}.

She reduces the Cooldown of {{Spell_KarmaMantra_Name}} by [4] seconds when she damages a champion with an Ability.

Karma empowers her next Ability used within 8 seconds.
{{Spell_KarmaQ_Name}}: Deals an additional [40 / 100 / 160 / 220 + (0.3) × AP] magic damage and leaves behind a circle of flame, Slowing enemies and dealing an additional [40 / 130 / 220 / 310 + (0.5) × AP] magic damage.{{Spell_KarmaSpiritBind_Name}}: Karma will restore [(17 + (0.01) × AP) × (0.01)] missing Health at the beginning and end of the tether, and Root for [0.5 / 0.75 / 1 / 1.25]s longer.{{Spell_KarmaSolKimShield_Name}}: Karma shields her target for [45 / 85 / 125 / 165 + (0.45) × AP] more Shield, and also shields allies near her target, granting them [(45 / 85 / 125 / 165 + (0.45) × AP) × (1)] Shield and [15]% Move Speed.

builds.name: Renewal missing-health duelist
builds.summary: Use two Mantra-W heal timings rather than a single poke cycle.
builds.goal: Use two Mantra-W heal timings rather than a single poke cycle.
builds.hypothesis: Renewal heals an AP-linked percentage of missing health at both tether start and completion; normal W must stay linked for two seconds to root. Visage amplifies healing received, Rod supports mana/health, and Cosmic Drive plus Inspire speed helps preserve tether. Ability damage reduces Mantra cooldown by four seconds, enabling a pressure-dependent next renewal.
testPlan: Required state: Need missing health without lethal risk, unbroken tether and actual champion ability hits.
Compare both heal events, Mantra cooldown and survival versus a mobile melee target.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Anti-heal, burst before the first heal or a broken tether removes the second payoff.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Mantra's heal is not flat max-health healing and a broken tether does not grant the completion heal.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Rod of Ages, Spirit Visage, Cosmic Drive, Riftmaker, Rabadon's Deathcap, Mercury's Treads. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Protection specialist
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Karma: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A flexible poke and protection mage who chooses between empowered damage, tether healing and multi-ally shields. Separate Mantra Q poke, W recovery and E team shields. An AP-health route must justify tether uptime and protection loss rather than granting every Mantra option simultaneously. Healing/shield power and timed actives test preserving an allied carry.
builds.summary: Healing/shield power and timed actives test preserving an allied carry.
testPlan: Kit question for Karma: Separate Mantra Q poke, W recovery and E team shields. An AP-health route must justify tether uptime and protection loss rather than granting every Mantra option simultaneously.

Start with the early core (Support quest, Moonstone only with useful eligible heals/shields, then the needed active) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use real support income and keep the quest/vision slot.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Healing/shield power and timed actives test preserving an allied carry. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Karma sends forth a ball of spirit energy that explodes and deals damage upon hitting an enemy unit.

Mantra Bonus: In addition to the explosion, Mantra increases the destructive power of her Inner Flame, creating a cataclysm which deals damage after a short delay. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Only eligible heals/shields benefit; carrying too many actives can reduce practical value.

The route fails Karma's stated kit question: Separate Mantra Q poke, W recovery and E team shields. An AP-health route must justify tether uptime and protection loss rather than granting every Mantra option simultaneously.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility. Also record allies lost while spending on personal damage.
tradeoffs: Only eligible heals/shields benefit; carrying too many actives can reduce practical value.
Full cost 10,600 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Support quest, Moonstone only with useful eligible heals/shields, then the needed active. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Begin with the actual support quest item; Celestial Opposition is earned by transformation, not directly bought as a 400-gold legendary. Keep buying vision.
Redemption, Mikael's Blessing, Dawncore are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.name: Inspire AP transfer engine
builds.summary: Let offensive hits finance repeated multi-ally shield windows.
builds.goal: Let offensive hits finance repeated multi-ally shield windows.
builds.hypothesis: Inspire's base shield has 0.6 AP; Mantra adds 0.45 AP shielding and spreads protection to allies. Staff supplies temporary AP/haste after an allied shield, Moonstone can chain shields, and Helia spends damage-earned charges when shielding. Gathering Fire makes well-timed Q/W champion hits valuable before the next defensive Mantra, rather than substituting auto attacks for documented refunds.
testPlan: Required state: Need grouped allies for empowered E and safe actual spell damage between shield casts.
Measure primary and nearby shields plus Mantra uptime in a repeated poke-and-protect sequence.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Mana pressure or threat forces pure shielding, slowing Mantra refunds and Helia charge gains.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Every allied shield is not an independent infinite Helia charge source; charges must be earned first.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
